idea: Develop the bishop toward f7 and prepare a supported central pawn break.
whitePlan: Castle, support e4, and prepare d4 when your pieces can use the opened centre.
blackPlan: Develop actively, secure the king, and contest the centre with a well-timed ...d5.
watch: An attack on f7 needs concrete support; the bishop alone does not win the pawn.

positions.title: Italian Game: key idea
positions.prompt: Prepare to support a later d4 advance.
positions.explanation: c3 supports d4. In this quiet line White then uses d3 to secure e4 before opening the centre.

idea: Pressure the knight that defends e5, then build central pressure while developing.
whitePlan: Secure the king and support e4 before preparing c3 and d4 in the closed structures.
blackPlan: Develop, defend the centre, and choose when to challenge the bishop or release central tension.
watch: Bxc6 followed by Nxe5 does not automatically win a pawn; Black has tactical resources.

positions.title: Ruy Lopez: key idea
positions.prompt: Your bishop has retreated and Black has developed. Secure your king.
positions.explanation: O-O castles and activates the rook. White can now reinforce the centre instead of starting an unsupported attack.

idea: Open the centre early and use active piece development.
whitePlan: Recapture on d4 with a piece, develop the remaining pieces, and castle.
blackPlan: Use the open lines to develop quickly and put pressure on e4.
watch: Repeated moves by the central knight can let the opponent catch up in development.

positions.title: Scotch Game: key idea
positions.prompt: Challenge e5 directly with a central pawn.
positions.explanation: d4 opens the centre. After ...exd4, Nxd4 places the knight actively while recovering the pawn.

idea: Black attacks e4 instead of immediately defending e5.
whitePlan: Use central space and natural development to test Black without assuming the symmetry means a draw.
blackPlan: Challenge the advanced knight before recovering the pawn, then support the centre.
watch: Immediate ...Nxe4 after Nxe5 allows Qe2 with awkward threats.

positions.title: Petroff Defence: key idea
positions.prompt: Drive the e5 knight away before recovering the e4 pawn.
positions.explanation: d6 attacks Ne5. After Nf3, ...Nxe4 recovers the pawn in this standard move order.

idea: Black uses a pawn to hold e5, accepting less space for a solid centre.
whitePlan: Claim space with d4 and develop into the centre before launching an attack.
blackPlan: Complete development and seek a freeing central break when prepared.
watch: A compact setup needs active development; defending everything passively leaves little room.

positions.title: Philidor Defence: key idea
positions.prompt: Take more central space while challenging e5.
positions.explanation: d4 attacks e5. The exchange shown here opens lines and lets White recapture with the knight.

idea: White develops the queenside knight first and keeps several central setups available.
whitePlan: Develop, secure the king, and choose between a quiet centre and a prepared f4 advance.
blackPlan: Meet White with natural development and look for a well-supported ...d5 break.
watch: The f-pawn advance changes king safety; do not play it automatically in every Vienna position.

positions.title: Vienna Game: key idea
positions.prompt: Develop the light bishop toward f7 in this quiet Vienna line.
positions.explanation: Bc4 develops with pressure toward f7. White retains choices about the central pawns rather than committing immediately to a gambit.

idea: Both sides develop their knights before choosing a bishop setup or central break.
whitePlan: Coordinate development, then use d4 or bishop pressure to influence the centre.
blackPlan: Keep developing and answer central threats before copying White automatically.
watch: Symmetry does not make every mirrored move safe; checks and captures can change the position.

positions.title: Four Knights Game: key idea
positions.prompt: Bring your second knight toward the centre.
positions.explanation: Nc3 develops the b1 knight and protects e4. Black can complete the four-knight setup with ...Nf6.

idea: White offers the f-pawn to challenge e5 and accelerate activity.
whitePlan: Develop quickly and handle king safety while trying to recover the pawn or use the open lines.
blackPlan: Consolidate with development; decide whether holding the extra pawn is worth the time.
watch: The opened king diagonal makes careless attacking moves costly.

positions.title: King's Gambit: key idea
positions.prompt: Develop the kingside knight and control h4 after Black accepts the pawn.
positions.explanation: Nf3 develops and controls h4, making a direct ...Qh4+ unavailable. White still needs rapid development to justify the pawn offer.

idea: White develops the bishop early, leaving the kingside knight flexible.
whitePlan: Support e4, develop the knights, and choose the moment for central expansion.
blackPlan: Attack the centre with development and prepare ...d5 when possible.
watch: Pressure on f7 is a theme, not a licence to sacrifice without calculation.

positions.title: Bishop's Opening: key idea
positions.prompt: Support e4 with a pawn and open a path for the other bishop.
positions.explanation: d3 protects e4 and opens the c1 bishop diagonal. White can continue developing behind a stable centre.

idea: Black contests the centre with the c-pawn, creating an asymmetric structure.
whitePlan: In the Open Sicilian, use the central knight and development lead to create activity.
blackPlan: Develop around the chosen pawn structure and use central breaks and the half-open c-file.
watch: Najdorf, Dragon, Closed and Alapin positions need different plans; learn a branch before memorising deep lines.

positions.title: Sicilian Defence: key idea
positions.prompt: Open the centre in this Open Sicilian line.
positions.explanation: d4 invites ...cxd4 and Nxd4. White trades the d-pawn for Black's c-pawn and develops an active central knight.

idea: A supported ...d5 challenges White; in the Advance structure the pawn chains define the plans.
whitePlan: Support the d4 base, develop, and use the extra space without neglecting the king.
blackPlan: Attack d4 with ...c5 and pieces; look for a useful role for the light bishop.
watch: Pushing more pawns does not repair an undefended base on d4.

positions.title: French Defence: key idea
positions.prompt: Challenge the base of White's pawn chain.
positions.explanation: c5 attacks d4, the support for e5. After c3, ...Nc6 adds another attacker to the same target.

idea: Black prepares ...d5 while leaving the light bishop a route outside the pawn chain.
whitePlan: Use the space advantage, finish development, and watch Black's central breaks.
blackPlan: Develop the light bishop before ...e6 in this Advance setup, then challenge the centre.
watch: The bishop move order matters: ...e6 first closes the route from c8 to f5.

positions.title: Caro-Kann Defence: key idea
positions.prompt: Develop the light bishop before closing its diagonal.
positions.explanation: Bf5 brings the c8 bishop outside the pawn chain. Black can then play ...e6 without trapping it behind the pawns.

idea: Black challenges e4 immediately; a queen recapture gives White a developing target.
whitePlan: Develop with tempo against the queen, take central space, and complete development.
blackPlan: Move the queen to a useful safe square and develop efficiently around the centre.
watch: Chasing the queen repeatedly can waste the time gained by the first developing attack.

positions.title: Scandinavian Defence: key idea
positions.prompt: Develop a knight while attacking the queen.
positions.explanation: Nc3 develops and attacks Qd5. Once the queen moves, White can use d4 to occupy the centre.

idea: Black allows a broad white centre and prepares to challenge it with pieces and pawn breaks.
whitePlan: Develop behind the centre and choose a setup that keeps the king safe.
blackPlan: Fianchetto, castle, and choose an appropriate ...c5 or ...e5 challenge.
watch: Having space is useful only if the centre can withstand counterattack.

positions.title: Pirc Defence: key idea
positions.prompt: Complete the kingside fianchetto.
positions.explanation: Bg7 develops the bishop onto the long diagonal. Black is preparing to castle and contest the centre.

idea: Black fianchettoes before committing the g8 knight, preserving move-order choices.
whitePlan: Occupy the centre, develop naturally, and watch for attacks on the pawn chain.
blackPlan: Use the long diagonal and choose central breaks according to White's setup.
watch: Delaying development too long gives White time to consolidate the space advantage.

positions.title: Modern Defence: key idea
positions.prompt: Use the square prepared by ...g6 to develop the bishop.
positions.explanation: Bg7 completes the fianchetto. The bishop will exert more influence when central pawns move or are exchanged.

idea: Black invites pawn advances and then attacks the extended centre.
whitePlan: Gain space while developing enough pieces to support the pawns.
blackPlan: Keep the knight safe and undermine the advanced pawns with timely central breaks.
watch: Chasing the knight with every pawn can create targets and leave pieces undeveloped.

positions.title: Alekhine's Defence: key idea
positions.prompt: Challenge the advanced e5 pawn with the d-pawn.
positions.explanation: d6 attacks e5, beginning the counterattack against White's advanced centre. Black must keep developing as the tension changes.

idea: Black reinforces d5 with ...e6 and builds a solid central structure.
whitePlan: Develop with pressure on d5 and choose when to exchange the c-pawn.
blackPlan: Develop, secure the king, and prepare a freeing ...c5 or suitable central exchange.
watch: The light bishop needs a development plan because the e6 pawn blocks its diagonal.

positions.title: Queen's Gambit Declined: key idea
positions.prompt: Support d5 with the e-pawn.
positions.explanation: e6 reinforces d5 and opens the f8 bishop diagonal. The c8 bishop is restricted, a trade-off Black must address later.

idea: Black takes the c4 pawn and relies on activity to challenge White's centre.
whitePlan: Develop and recover c4 under favourable conditions, often using the f1 bishop.
blackPlan: Develop quickly and challenge the centre rather than spending many moves defending c4.
watch: Trying to keep the extra pawn at any cost can expose the queenside and delay development.

positions.title: Queen's Gambit Accepted: key idea
positions.prompt: Open a route for the bishop to recover c4.
positions.explanation: e3 supports d4 and opens the f1 bishop diagonal toward c4. White prepares to recover the pawn through development.

idea: Black supports d5 with the c-pawn, leaving the light bishop diagonal available.
whitePlan: Develop and maintain central pressure while watching Black's choices about ...dxc4.
blackPlan: Develop the pieces and choose when the light bishop can leave the pawn chain safely.
watch: A bishop move can leave b7 or d5 vulnerable; opening the diagonal is only the first step.

positions.title: Slav Defence: key idea
positions.prompt: Support d5 without moving the e-pawn.
positions.explanation: c6 reinforces d5 while keeping c8-h3 open. This gives Black a different bishop-development problem from the Queen's Gambit Declined.

idea: Black combines the ...c6 and ...e6 supports for d5, creating a strong but compact centre.
whitePlan: Develop the bishops and decide whether to keep central tension or resolve it.
blackPlan: Complete development and prepare a freeing ...c5 or ...e5 break.
watch: A solid pawn triangle can become passive if the pieces never find active squares.

positions.title: Semi-Slav Defence: key idea
positions.prompt: Add the e-pawn support to d5 in this Semi-Slav structure.
positions.explanation: e6 supports d5 and frees the f8 bishop. Black accepts a restricted light bishop while building a resilient centre.

idea: White develops the dark bishop before building an e3-based pawn chain.
whitePlan: Support the centre, develop, castle, and prepare e4 when the position permits.
blackPlan: Contest the centre with ...c5 or ...e5 and challenge White's comfortable setup.
watch: A familiar setup still requires checking threats; opponent moves can change the right move order.

positions.title: London System: key idea
positions.prompt: Develop the dark bishop outside the future e3 pawn chain.
positions.explanation: Bf4 places the bishop actively before e3 blocks its diagonal from c1. White can then support the centre and develop the other bishop.

idea: White develops behind a d4/e3 centre and prepares an eventual e4 break.
whitePlan: Coordinate the pieces, castle, and support e4 before opening the centre.
blackPlan: Challenge d4 with ...c5 and develop actively before White achieves the central break.
watch: The c1 bishop can remain cramped; the system needs a plan to open the position.

positions.title: Colle System: key idea
positions.prompt: Develop the light bishop to support the e4 break.
positions.explanation: Bd3 develops and controls e4. White should coordinate the remaining pieces before pushing the e-pawn.

idea: White combines the queen-pawn centre with a bishop on the long diagonal.
whitePlan: Develop, castle, and use the g2 bishop to pressure the centre and queenside.
blackPlan: Choose whether to hold d5 or take c4, while completing development and managing the long diagonal.
watch: Recovering a pawn should be balanced against development and the bishop's activity.

positions.title: Catalan Opening: key idea
positions.prompt: Place the bishop on the diagonal prepared by g3.
positions.explanation: Bg2 completes the fianchetto and points toward the central d5 square. Its pressure grows as the centre opens.

idea: Black pins the c3 knight and contests e4 with pieces.
whitePlan: Develop and decide how to handle the pin, possible doubled pawns, and the bishop pair.
blackPlan: Use the pin and central pressure; exchange on c3 only when it serves the position.
watch: The bishop pair and pawn structure are trade-offs, not automatic advantages in every position.

positions.title: Nimzo-Indian Defence: key idea
positions.prompt: Pin the c3 knight to restrict its influence on e4.
positions.explanation: Bb4 pins Nc3 to the king and helps Black control e4. Black may later exchange bishop for knight or keep the tension.

idea: Black develops the light bishop on the long diagonal to influence central squares.
whitePlan: Develop and look for chances to expand with d5 or e4 under favourable conditions.
blackPlan: Use the bishop and knights to restrain the centre, then prepare an appropriate pawn break.
watch: A long diagonal can be blocked by your own pieces; coordinate them to keep the bishop useful.

positions.title: Queen's Indian Defence: key idea
positions.prompt: Complete the queenside fianchetto.
positions.explanation: Bb7 develops the light bishop toward e4. The bishop and f6 knight can cooperate to contest central space.

idea: Black develops with check before White commits the queenside knight.
whitePlan: Meet the check with development and continue building a coordinated centre.
blackPlan: Decide whether to exchange the bishop or retreat it while keeping development efficient.
watch: A check is useful only if the resulting position supports your plan.

positions.title: Bogo-Indian Defence: key idea
positions.prompt: Block the check with a developing bishop move.
positions.explanation: Bd2 interposes the c1 bishop and challenges Bb4. White develops while meeting the immediate threat.

idea: Black allows White a broad centre and prepares counterplay against it.
whitePlan: Develop behind the space advantage and respond to Black's central breaks.
blackPlan: Castle, finish development, and choose between ...e5 and ...c5 according to the structure.
watch: A kingside pawn storm belongs to particular closed structures; it is not the plan in every variation.

positions.title: King's Indian Defence: key idea
positions.prompt: Control e5 and prepare a central challenge.
positions.explanation: d6 restrains e5 and prepares a later ...e5 break. Black should coordinate development and king safety before committing to an attack.

idea: Black challenges the centre immediately and may allow a large white pawn centre as a target.
whitePlan: Support the central pawns with pieces and use the space to develop actively.
blackPlan: Attack the centre with the g7 bishop, pawn breaks, and coordinated pieces.
watch: A large pawn centre can be strong or vulnerable depending on piece support.

positions.title: Grünfeld Defence: key idea
positions.prompt: Challenge d4 immediately with a central pawn.
positions.explanation: d5 contests the centre. In the Exchange line that follows, White gains a broad pawn centre that Black will try to undermine.

idea: The asymmetric pawn structure gives White central space and Black queenside counterplay.
whitePlan: Support the d5 pawn, develop, and prepare e4-e5 when it can be sustained.
blackPlan: Develop actively and seek counterplay, often using a queenside pawn break.
watch: Black's cramped position needs activity; White should not allow counterplay without checking it.

positions.title: Modern Benoni: key idea
positions.prompt: Challenge the advanced d5 pawn with the e-pawn.
positions.explanation: e6 puts pressure on d5. After exchanges, the remaining white d5 pawn gives space while Black seeks activity around it.

idea: Black offers a queenside pawn to open files and gain sustained piece activity.
whitePlan: Balance the extra pawn against development and queenside pressure; returning material can be a useful option.
blackPlan: Develop the bishop and rooks toward the opened queenside files.
watch: This pawn offer seeks lasting pressure; it does not promise an immediate tactical win.

positions.title: Benko Gambit: key idea
positions.prompt: Offer the b-pawn to start opening the queenside.
positions.explanation: b5 challenges c4 and offers a pawn. After cxb5, ...a6 continues the plan of opening lines for the black pieces.

idea: Black controls e4 with the f-pawn and accepts changes to king safety.
whitePlan: Develop and challenge Black's centre while watching the squares weakened by ...f5.
blackPlan: Build a coordinated setup and secure the king before using the kingside space.
watch: The f-pawn move opens lines around the king; do not neglect development.

positions.title: Dutch Defence: key idea
positions.prompt: Use the f-pawn to contest e4 in the Dutch.
positions.explanation: f5 controls e4 and gains kingside space. It also changes king safety, so Black must develop carefully.

idea: White controls central squares from the flank and keeps the central pawns flexible.
whitePlan: Develop the fianchetto and choose a central break based on Black's structure.
blackPlan: Contest central squares and avoid copying moves when the position calls for a concrete response.
watch: The English reaches many structures; plans depend on whether Black uses ...e5, ...c5, or another setup.

positions.title: English Opening: key idea
positions.prompt: Prepare the bishop for the long diagonal.
positions.explanation: g3 prepares Bg2 while leaving the d- and e-pawns flexible. This is a common development plan in the Symmetrical English.

idea: White develops first and then challenges the centre from the side.
whitePlan: Pressure d5, develop flexibly, and decide when to occupy the centre with pawns.
blackPlan: Use the available space, develop, and support the centre against flank pressure.
watch: Move orders can transpose into other openings; recognise the structure rather than relying only on the name.

positions.title: Réti Opening: key idea
positions.prompt: Challenge the d5 pawn with your c-pawn.
positions.explanation: c4 attacks d5 from the flank. White can then decide how to develop and whether to enter a queen-pawn structure.

idea: White develops the dark bishop early and challenges the f6 knight.
whitePlan: Use flexible development and decide whether exchanging on f6 helps your central plan.
blackPlan: Meet the bishop actively while maintaining development and central control.
watch: A trade on f6 changes the pawn structure but also gives up a bishop; assess both consequences.

positions.title: Trompowsky Attack: key idea
positions.prompt: Develop the dark bishop to challenge Nf6.
positions.explanation: Bg5 attacks the knight before White commits the c-pawn. It introduces the choice of exchanging on f6 or retaining the bishop.
